name: the least edge count of a host graph forcing

phase_0.boundary_condition: the minimal edge count of a host graph that forces a monochromatic copy of a given graph
phase_0.domain_name: the least edge count of a host graph forcing
phase_0.justification: Auto-designed by the native Ob3ect Auto-Designer (in-process candle, no Python)

AFWD.chosen_element: incrementing the edge count toward a larger candidate host
AFWD.justification: forward morphism that advances the search from one edge count to the next, exploring the space of possible host graphs.

AREV.chosen_element: reversion after a failed candidate graph
AREV.justification: contravariant step that discards a host graph that does not force H, returning to the pool of candidates with increased edge number.

CLINK.chosen_element: chaining the forcing verification with the minimality verification
CLINK.justification: composition that concatenates the proof that the candidate G forces H and the proof that no smaller graph does so, building the full argument.

ENGAGR.chosen_element: the simultaneous assertion of existence and non-existence of a minimal host graph
ENGAGR.justification: holds both the T and F branches live at once, representing a contradiction that is not resolved away but kept as the paraconsistent B verdict.

EVALF.chosen_element: the statement that no host graph with k' edges forces H
EVALF.justification: constructive negation that asserts the impossibility of a forcing host with fewer edges; used to confirm the candidate k is genuinely minimal.

EVALT.chosen_element: a specific host graph G with k edges that forces a monochromatic copy of H
EVALT.justification: constructive affirmation that such a graph exists and successfully forces the target under every red/blue coloring of its edges.

FFUSE.chosen_element: the final join of the existence and non-existence arms
FFUSE.justification: rejoins the two branches into a single resolved verdict; if both arms carry contradictory evidence the fusion yields B, the paraconsistent B4 value.

FSPLIT.chosen_element: the main existence fork: a minimal host graph exists vs. none exists
FSPLIT.justification: splits the problem into two complementary arms; one arm constructs a minimal forcer, the other arm establishes that the set of forcing edge counts has no minimum.

IFIX.chosen_element: the recorded minimal host graph and its edge count, or the recorded impossibility
IFIX.justification: irreversible, append-only fixation of the structural object into the permanent mathematical record.

IMSCRIB.justification: self-referential benchmark; every host graph is judged by whether it forces a monochromatic copy of this fixed structure.

TANCH.chosen_element: the closed verdict on the least forcing edge count
TANCH.justification: the terminal anchor seals the entire resolution, containing the final answer as a single B4 state.

VINIT.justification: the size Ramsey problem begins with no host graph, no edge count, and no candidate structure.

phase_2.fuse_element: the final verdict on the size Ramsey number
phase_2.fuse_result: a single B4 state (N, T, F, or B) that resolves the existence claim
phase_2.rejoin_note: Inside the existence arm, a nested FSPLIT/FFUSE pair verifies the forcing property over all red/blue colorings of G, and another nested pair checks minimality over all smaller edge counts; if any coloring fails to produce a monochromatic H or any smaller graph itself forces H, the inner fusion produces B, which propagates to the outer fusion, potentially leading to a B resolution. The arms rejoin to a single resolved state whose exact B4 value is computed by the kernel over SIXTEEN_3.
phase_2.split_input: the problem statement after the target graph H is fixed
split_outputs: affirmative arm: a minimal host graph G exists with some edge count k
negative arm: no such minimal host graph exists
phase_2.verdict_reason: Tri-ancestral reconnection over a transformed object — closes

phase_3.both_description: B4 B (11) — both held at once: a contradiction arises, e.g., from a host graph that simultaneously forces and fails to force H, or from incompatible existence and non-existence proofs. This is the paraconsistent resolution.
phase_3.false_description: B4 F (10) — constructively refuted: no minimal host graph exists; the set of edge counts of host graphs that force H has no least element.
phase_3.true_description: B4 T (01) — constructively proven: a minimal host graph G exists and its edge count k is identified as the size Ramsey number.
phase_3.void_description: B4 N (00) — neither established: the problem is uninitialized, no candidate host or edge count exists.

steps.domain_action: The domain is void; the problem of finding the least forcing edge count has no host graph, no edge count, and no coloring yet defined.
The target graph H is fixed as the self-referential identity; every subsequent check will test for a monochromatic copy of this graph.
Begin the structured search by considering edge count zero, moving forward through increasing natural numbers.
For each edge count that admits no forcing host graph, backtrack to discard it and advance to the next count.
Branch into the two definitional cases: a minimal host graph exists (affirmative arm) or no such graph exists (negative arm).
Affirmative arm — a minimal host graph G with some edge count k will be constructed and verified.
Advance to the specific candidate minimal edge count k and select a host graph G with exactly k edges.
Reverse past all host graphs with fewer edges that failed to force H, confirming that k is the first viable candidate.
To verify the forcing property, split over all red/blue colorings of the edges of G.
For each coloring arm, assert that a monochromatic copy of H is present — reflecting that G is a true forcer.
Fuse the outcomes of the coloring arms; if every coloring yields EVALT the fusion confirms that G forces H, otherwise contradictory values produce a mixed verdict.
Chain the verified forcing of G into the next verification stage: proving that no smaller graph forces H.
Proceed to the minimality check; for every edge count k' less than k, assert that no host graph with k' edges forces H.
Branch over all smaller edge counts k' < k, each representing the claim that no forcer exists at that size.
For each k', assert the statement "there exists a host graph with k' edges that forces H" is false; this denies the existence of a smaller forcer.
Fuse the minimality verifications across all k'; the rejoin establishes that no smaller edge count works, confirming that k is the genuine minimum.
Permanently record the minimal host graph G and its edge count k as the definitive size Ramsey structural object.
Negative arm — assert that no minimal host graph exists; the least forcing edge count is undefined.
Record the impossibility as a permanent negative result in the mathematical record.
Compose the outcomes of the two arms — if both hold evidence, they will be composed into a single paraconsistent chain.
Fuse the affirmative and negative arms into one resolved verdict on the existence of the minimal host graph.
In the event that both arms are supported, hold the contradiction live as the B state.
Seal the boundary; the entire structural object — the least edge count forcing a monochromatic copy — is now closed and resolved.

phase_5.alfs_store: the Erdős corpus index of known Ramsey bounds and referenced theorems, providing the canonical bootstrap store for this domain
phase_5.compiler_frontend: the combinatorial search procedure that translates the target graph H into a systematic enumeration of candidate host graphs and colorings
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: message passing between the forcing verifier (coloring split) and the minimality checker (edge-count split), exchanging verdict fragments
phase_5.memory_mechanism: a store of already evaluated host graphs, their edge counts, and the outcomes of their coloring splits to avoid recomputation
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: the well-ordering of natural numbers, which determines the order in which edge counts are examined from smallest to largest

phase_6.cycle_cost: the computational work of enumerating all colorings of a candidate host graph and checking for a monochromatic copy of H
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — the thermal cost of evaluating and discarding candidates is exactly returned in the form of the fixed structural record; no net entropy is produced, as the resolution conserves the total informational budget.
phase_6.post_cycle_state: a single verified minimal host graph recorded permanently, or a recorded impossibility; all candidate information is collapsed into a resolved structural object
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: a pool of unevaluated host graphs with various edge counts, and an unknown minimal edge count
